evidence.source: 漢語多功能字庫, Chinese University of Hong Kong
evidence.field: 地; form analysis and cited noun/particle uses
evidence.text: The entry analyzes 地 as 土 meaning component plus 也 sound component. It quotes Shuowen’s earth/heaven explanation and cites 易·繫辭下 for earth, 詩·小雅·斯干 for ground, 周禮 for land and territory, 管子 for place, 孟子 for status, Tang 李白 for distance, and Song 張先 for adjective-following 地. These are citations to texts, not independent dates of their compositions or surviving witnesses; they do not establish a complete semantic path.
evidence.title: 漢語多功能字庫

evidence.field: 地-bronze.svg; script identification, source and rights
evidence.text: The page describes a digitally drawn vector representation of 地 in Western Zhou bronze script and identifies the source as Academia Sinica Xiaoxuetang record 34.E059 associated with 㝬簋, late Western Zhou. It states that this image is CC0 1.0. This is a modern redraw, not a photograph of the ancient inscription.
evidence.title: File:地-bronze.svg - Wikimedia Commons

evidence.field: 地-seal.svg; script identification, source and rights
evidence.text: The page describes a digitally drawn vector representation of 地 in Shuowen seal script. It identifies Xiaoxuetang image 27.5730 as one source and states CC0 1.0 for the Sinica database image and Commons file. This is a modern redraw of a seal-script form, not an ancient artifact photograph.
evidence.title: File:地-seal.svg - Wikimedia Commons

search_audit.query: 地 字形演变 西周 金文 小學堂 Academia Sinica 地; Wikimedia Commons 地 Chinese character bronze script image; site:humanum.arts.cuhk.edu.hk/Lexis/lexi-mf 地 从土也声
search_audit.outcome: Fresh web search inspected relevant Xiaoxuetang, CUHK, and Commons pages. Search results for the CUHK target were noisy; the specific 地 entry was opened separately and its analysis and cited examples inspected.

search_audit.query: Open Xiaoxuetang 地 query, Shuowen 土部 text, CUHK 地 entry, Wikimedia Commons 地 category
search_audit.outcome: Opened the pages. The selected Xiaoxuetang query rendered only its generic interface; the CUHK entry provided a readable analysis and examples. The Wikisource page opened but its target entry was not located in the returned extracted text.

search_audit.query: Inspect 地-bronze.svg and 地-seal.svg Commons descriptions and originals
search_audit.outcome: Both Commons description pages were inspected and state source and CC0 rights. Retrieval of the bronze original failed with cache miss; the seal original was rejected by the web tool for SVG content type. No pixel inspection was performed.

gaps: No primary inscription image or archaeological publication was inspected in this invocation. The Commons candidates are secondary modern redrawings; their source pages identify the underlying records but this pass did not inspect those pixels.

The Xiaoxuetang character query loaded only a generic interface, so no direct database image candidate or specific record page is proposed. Its official CC0 notice was not independently opened in this invocation.
The Shuowen page opened, but extracted text did not reveal the 地 entry during this pass; the dossier already contains a separately documented transcription, which is not fresh verification.

The CUHK examples attest a range of cited noun senses and a Song particle citation, but cited classical works do not by themselves date the surviving wording. The semantic links and earliest attestations remain unresolved.

No new source in this pass independently established the historical sound relation of 地 and 也; use dossier phonology evidence with its system and reconstruction limits. The original referent/name of 也 remains uncertain, without negating its later phonetic role.
The proposed bronze image direct-file URL could not be retrieved by the web tool. The source page nevertheless provided a direct original-file link, but the harness should handle the SVG URL itself.

items.period: Late Western Zhou, associated with 㝬簋
items.caption: A modern vector redraw of a 地 form sourced to Xiaoxuetang record 34.E059 (㝬簋). It gives a dated-script comparison for the early graph, but does not by itself settle its component reading.
items.alt: Modern black vector drawing of an early bronze-script form of 地.
items.selection_reason: The source page identifies the underlying late Western Zhou record, source database and CC0 status; an early comparator is useful for discussing form history while clearly marking this as a redraw.
items.rights: CC0 1.0, as stated on the Commons page for the representation and its cited Xiaoxuetang source image.

items.period: Shuowen seal-script tradition; dictionary compiled in the Eastern Han (c. 100 CE)
items.caption: A modern vector redraw of the Shuowen seal-script form, identified by Commons as sourced in part to Xiaoxuetang record 27.5730. It illustrates the transmitted lexicographic form, not a Han artifact photograph.
items.alt: Modern vector drawing of 地 in seal-script style.
items.selection_reason: Pairs an identified early bronze-script redraw with the seal-script form referenced in the received Shuowen account; the source page gives provenance and rights.
items.rights: CC0 1.0, as stated on the Commons page; the specific Sinica image is also identified there as CC0.

limitations.text: Both candidates are modern vector redrawings. Their labels and educational captions do not claim direct visual inspection of ancient artifact images or the files' pixels.

The underlying Academia Sinica record pages were not independently rendered in usable form here. The specific source record identifiers and rights attribution are reported by the Commons file descriptions.
